analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and file metadata against the indexed threat model, including detailed T-041. FlintNativeProtocolConstraint.swift:148-162 adds per-state mask keys and opts into speculative chained decoding. Its allowed set depends only on immutable request rules, interned boundary and positive budget; existing state limits and fail-closed transitions remain intact (:164-184). FlintAnswerStopConstraint.swift:70-91 delegates scanning keys to the base and assigns matched masks key -1; these keys agree with the visible allowedTokenIDs implementation (:55-67). No concrete regression is established locally.
FlintAnswerStopTests.swift head patch :197-209 checks equal masks for shared keys and zero-budget rejection, but not sampler integration. EngineV2KVBackendPolicyTests.swift:31,258-269 adds Flint paged-selection and M5 serving-width expectations; surrounding tests retain resident-prefix-cache exclusion, overrides, fallback and headroom expectations. These tests alone do not establish production backend behavior or changes to T-041's SSD account scoping, encryption or donation policy.
Material integration questions under TB-007, T-007, T-010, T-028 and T-041: verify the CBv2 sampler namespaces mask caches per constraint/request, accepts negative cache keys, bounds device-mask retention, and invalidates speculative work using confirmed constraint state rather than mask-key equality. Stop-progress states can share a mask key while having different transitions. Confirm redraw/termination preserve token accounting, stop filtering, cancellation and fail-closed resource exhaustion. Review production Flint paged/concurrency changes with actual KV allocation and cache bindings. Those implementations are outside this supplied scope; their absence is not evidence of a missing control. No visible changes affect authorization, attestation, transport encryption, credentials or privileged-helper authority.
